newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 1997 budget deficit seen $37 bln - Clinton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 1997 budget deficit seen $37 bln - Clinton.

text.p: The U.S. budget deficit for the current fiscal year is expected to be just $37 billion, President Bill Clinton announced on Wednesday.

"Today I have some more good news. Our efforts have led to an even lower budget deficit than we projected...we now expect the deficit to drop to $37 billion," Clinton told reporters at a news conference.
"Yet without the bipartisan balanced budget we just passed, my budget officials estimate the defict would rise next year to $50-$100 billion and stay at that level for years to come," he said.

Clinton on Tuesday signed legislation to balance the budget by 2002 and give Americans a tax cut. But critics say the growing economy deserves much of the credit for cutting the deficit and say that growth must continue if the United States is to get out of the red.
The federal budget has been in deficit every year since 1969. When Clinton took office in 1992 the deficit was a hefty $290 billion but it has steadily declined since then.
For fiscal 1996, that ended last Sept. 30, the shortfall was $107 billion after a $164 billion gap the year before that.
